So maybe you don't fish but you want to fish, but your worried about investing a shit load of money into a hobby you may not even get into or have time for. Guess what? It's not so bad. All you need to get started is a decent rod and reel and some tackle geared to the fish in your area.

A general almost universal place to start is a spinning rod and reel, this is my go to rig ALWAYS. Usually I would recommend a 7ft medium action rod, that's my only advice, fibreglass or graphite doesn't matter both are strong and castable. I buy whatever rods and reels are on clearence special because it doesn't mean they are bad it means they are old, me and my son got new rods and reels this year and I paid like 120$ Canadian total.(I got a quantum strike rod and reel, and he got a shimano LX2000 trigger reel and a berkley lightning rod).

Basic tackle go for a jigging setup(jigheads and softbaits, I like grubs), you can add a worm or minnow or leech as bait to them or just use a jig alone.

Spoons and spinners these are my favourites except the trebel hooks are prone to snags(most snags are solvable with the right techniques), but spoons and spinners are usually bright and flashy and they are slightly off shape so they emit vibrations that attract fishes attention, They are generally a great casting lure or a trolling lure with weights added. You can add ive baits but it's not necessary and I'm not sure if it even matters most times, for walleye with a spinner though I hiighly recommend a leech.

Last basic method is Bobber fishing, I recommend a slip bobber and any type of bobber stope, I use the little plastic football ones because locally I can get them cheaper then other types, but a slip bobber easily lets you adjust to various depths pretty much instantaniously, Always use live baits and a sinker or wighted jighead with a bobber. With slip bobbers if your bait is on the bottom they will generally lay sideways then you adjust the stopper closer to the bait, you want to be 1-3ft above bottom with a bobber generally.

Any more questions or input bring it on.

What's your technique for dealing with snags?

Also what do you recommend for getting a fish off the hook? They've always flailed around too much on me to do it properly not to mention being overcome like a weak willed faggot for seeing them suffer makes me panic and prolong the experience on them. Is there a gloves and plier combo type deal I should look into or is it more of a stop being a sissy thing and just fuckin do it?

To free snags my go to trick is to keep tension on the rod, but instead of jerking like a wildman I grab the line between the reel and the first eye and pull it out isideways and let go, it gives the line a nice snapping motion, try that a couple times, and if it doesn't work change directions, if your bank fishing from shore walk around trying it at different angles, usually it'll pop right out.

As for handling and unhooking fish, a lot of people use gloves, my brother developed a fish slime allergy when he was in his mid 30's and always has to wear a glove now or he busts out in hives. Pliers are essential, not only for your safety but for the fish as well. After you go through it a few times fish won't surprise or freak you out anymore then you can decide whether to keep using the glove or going bare handed.

Also fish don't really suffer, many times I've recaught fish seconds to minutes after releasing them. They are instinct driven not emotion driven, just be as gentle as realistically possible with them so when you release them they can carry on with their fish stuff.
